scan.summary: This is Oregon DEQ's Standard Air Contaminant Discharge Permit for the Portland facility. It allows you to run two acid/caustic scrubbers and four solvent tanks vented to a carbon unit, as long as you meet the permit's conditions. Because it is the agency's own document, there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is that it expires November 15, 2026, 49 days from today, and the renewal application date the permit gives (July 18, 2026) has already passed. You need to confirm right away that a timely, complete renewal application actually reached DEQ.
scan.freshness_note: This is the 2021 permit and it is still in force today, but it expires in 49 days (2026-11-15). Both renewal filing dates have passed: July 18, 2026 (the permit's own 120-day date) and, working it out myself, May 19, 2026 (the 180-day date in the current rule, OAR 340-216-0040(2)(b)(C), for Standard ACDPs). Ask for three things: (1) a copy of the renewal application you submitted, with DEQ's receipt or completeness letter; (2) any renewed permit DEQ may already have issued; (3) any amendments issued since 2021. Under OAR 340-216-0082, if no timely and complete renewal application was filed, the permit ends automatically on the expiration date. After that, running the scrubbers and tanks would be unpermitted operation. If you cannot find proof of filing, contact DEQ Northwest Region now.

conditions.evidence_expected: The records for conditions 3.1–5.2 below; a copy of this permit kept on site

conditions.title: Do not operate after November 15, 2026 unless the permit has been renewed or a timely renewal application is on file

conditions.title: Submit a complete renewal application on or before July 18, 2026 (120 days before expiration)

conditions.title: Give DEQ written notice at least 60 days before a change in ownership, and before any change to a permitted source that would increase emissions

conditions.title: Inspect each scrubber's recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing and mist eliminator at least once per calendar quarter, recording the date, the inspector and any corrective action
conditions.evidence_expected: Quarterly inspection entries in the scrubber log for S-1 and S-2

conditions.title: Replace the carbon in C-1 at least every 12 months, or sooner if the weekly detector-tube check at the C-1 outlet shows breakthrough, and record each replacement
conditions.evidence_expected: Weekly detector-tube check records; carbon change-out records or vendor invoices with dates

conditions.title: Keep visible emissions from any permitted source at or below 20% opacity (no more than 3 minutes aggregate in any hour)
conditions.evidence_expected: Visible-emissions observation records if kept; excess-emission reports if any occurred

conditions.title: Submit an annual report by February 15 covering the previous calendar year: throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon replacement dates, excess emission events
conditions.evidence_expected: Copies of each annual report with proof of submission (2022–2026 filings)

conditions.title: Submit a semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
conditions.evidence_expected: Copies of each semi-annual report with proof of submission, including the July 31, 2026 report

conditions.title: Keep all permit records for at least five years and make them available to DEQ on request
conditions.evidence_expected: An organized archive of logs, reports and carbon records going back five years

conditions.title: Minimize emissions during any scrubber malfunction, including stopping the associated repackaging line until the scrubber is back in service
conditions.evidence_expected: Malfunction and shutdown records showing line stoppages; a written malfunction procedure (inferred good practice)

conditions.title: Notify DEQ within 24 hours of discovering any permit deviation, and send a written report within 15 days (cause, duration, corrective action)
conditions.evidence_expected: Deviation notification records (email or phone log) and the written 15-day reports

conditions.title: Permit may be modified, suspended or revoked for cause
conditions.evidence_expected: None to hold; this is an administrative provision

conditions.title: Pay the annual permit fee DEQ invoices, by the due date on the invoice
conditions.evidence_expected: DEQ fee invoices and proof of payment for each year

Things I am sure of: this is Oregon DEQ's permit for the Portland site; it was issued 2021-09-01; it expires 2026-11-15; the renewal date it states, 2026-07-18, has passed (I checked the 120-day arithmetic). Things I am less sure of: (1) Whether you filed a renewal. This document cannot show that, and it is the most important open question. (2) The renewal lead time. The permit says 120 days, but the current rule text (OAR 340-216-0040(2)(b)(C), https://regulations.justia.com/states/oregon/chapter-340/division-216/section-340-216-0040/) sets 180 days for Standard ACDPs, which works out to 2026-05-19 (my calculation). I cannot tell which DEQ would apply, or whether the rule said something different in 2021. Both dates have passed either way. (3) What happens if no timely application was filed: per OAR 340-216-0082 (https://oregon.public.law/rules/oar_340-216-0082), the permit ends automatically on the expiration date. (4) The roughly 5-year term is shorter than the 10-year maximum typical for ACDPs. That is DEQ's call and is not a problem with the document. (5) The Q4 2026 inspection due date and the "next" report dates are my own calculations from the condition wording. (6) I cannot tell from this document whether the permit was amended after 2021.

STATE OF OREGON
DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY
Northwest Region · 700 NE Multnomah Street, Suite 600, Portland, Oregon
97232
STANDARD AIR CONTAMINANT DISCHARGE PERMIT
Issued under OAR 340-216
Permit number: 26-2841-ST-01
Permittee: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC
Facility: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, Portland Facility
Facility address: 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Source category: Chemical storage and repackaging with vapor control
Date issued: September 1, 2021
Expiration date: November 15, 2026
This permit is issued in accordance with the provisions of ORS 468A.040 and OAR 340-216 and
authorizes the permittee to operate the air contaminant sources described below at the facility address,
subject to the conditions of this permit.
SECTION 1. GENERAL CONDITIONS
1.1 The permittee shall operate the sources listed in Section 2 in compliance with all conditions of this
permit and all applicable rules of the Department.
1.2 This permit expires on November 15, 2026. Operation of the permitted sources after the expiration
date without a renewed permit or a timely renewal application is a violation of this permit.
1.3 The permittee shall submit a complete application for renewal of this permit no later than 120 days
before the expiration date, that is, on or before July 18, 2026. A permittee that submits a timely and
complete renewal application may continue to operate under the terms of this permit until the Department
takes final action on the application.
1.4 The permittee shall notify the Department in writing at least 60 days before any change in ownership,
and before any modification to a permitted source that would increase emissions of any regulated
pollutant.
SECTION 2. PERMITTED SOURCES
2.1 Packed-bed wet scrubber S-1 serving the acid repackaging line (design flow 4,500 scfm).
2.2 Packed-bed wet scrubber S-2 serving the caustic repackaging line (design flow 3,000 scfm).
2.3 Solvent storage tanks T-3, T-4, T-5 and T-6 (each 10,000 gallons, fixed roof, vented to carbon
adsorption unit C-1).
SECTION 3. OPERATING AND MONITORING CONDITIONS
3.1 The permittee shall maintain the pressure drop across each scrubber S-1 and S-2 within the range of
2.0 to 6.0 inches of water column whenever the associated line is operating, and shall record the pressure
drop reading once per operating day in a scrubber log.
3.2 The permittee shall inspect each scrubber's recirculation pump, spray nozzles, packing and mist
eliminator at least once per calendar quarter and record the date, the inspector and any corrective action in
the scrubber log.
3.3 The permittee shall replace the carbon in adsorption unit C-1 at least once every 12 months or when
breakthrough is detected by the weekly detector-tube check at the C-1 outlet, whichever comes first, and
shall record each replacement.
3.4 Visible emissions from any permitted source shall not exceed 20 percent opacity for any period
aggregating more than three minutes in any one hour.
SECTION 4. RECORDKEEPING AND REPORTING
4.1 The permittee shall submit an annual report to the Department by February 15 of each year covering
the previous calendar year, including total throughput by line, scrubber log summaries, carbon
replacement dates and any excess emission events.
4.2 The permittee shall submit a semi-annual monitoring report by July 31 covering January through June
of the same year.
4.3 The permittee shall keep all records required by this permit for at least five years from the date of the
record and make them available to the Department on request.
SECTION 5. EXCESS EMISSIONS AND UPSETS
5.1 The permittee shall take all reasonable steps to minimize emissions during any period of scrubber
malfunction, including stopping the associated repackaging line until the scrubber is returned to service.
5.2 The permittee shall notify the Department by telephone or email within 24 hours of discovering any
deviation from a condition of this permit, and shall submit a written report within 15 days describing the
deviation, its cause, its duration and the corrective action taken.
SECTION 6. ADMINISTRATIVE
6.1 This permit may be modified, suspended or revoked for cause, including violation of any condition,
obtaining the permit by misrepresentation, or a change in any condition that requires reduction of the
permitted emissions.
6.2 The permittee shall pay the annual permit fee invoiced by the Department by the due date stated on
the invoice.
